column2: Wash the strawberries in plenty of water and remove the stalks; peel the banana.
Blend the yoghurt, milk, strawberries and banana until smooth.
Don't keep leftovers; throw them away.
Soak the bulgur in hot water for 10 minutes to swell; drain off excess water.
Knead the bulgur, mince, courgette and egg yolk for 3–4 minutes; then wash your hands.
Make small flat patties and arrange on the tray; bake for 20 minutes.
Meatballs must reach 71°C inside; cut one in half: no pink inside and the juices should run clear.
Peel and finely grate the apple and carrot; lightly squeeze the juice from the apple.
Mix the apple, carrot, oats, egg and cinnamon and leave for 10 minutes.
Drop small rounds onto the tray with a spoon and press to 1 cm thick.
Bake for 18 minutes until golden underneath.
Knead the mince and washed rice and form soft chickpea-sized balls; then wash your hands.
Add the meatballs; cook over low heat for 15 minutes until the rice is soft.
If you like, squeeze in a few drops of lemon.
Drain the boiled cauliflower well and mash with a fork.
Add the egg, breadcrumbs and cheese and knead; leave for 5 minutes.
Finely shred the boiled chicken.
Mix the drained pasta and chicken.
Melt the butter and drizzle it over the top.
Seed the pepper and chop very finely; wash the bulgur.
Add the pepper and tomato paste and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the bulgur and water; when it boils, cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Bring the chicken to the boil with the water and skim off the foam; cook over low heat for 20 minutes.
Take out the chicken and shred it finely.
Finely grate the carrot and add it to the cooking stock; cook for 5 minutes.
Pulse the corn briefly in a blender and add it.
Mix the flour with half a glass of cold water until lump-free and add to the pan.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring constantly; add the chicken.
Preheat the oven to 180°C; grease the mini tins.
Soak the white cheese in water for 1 hour to remove salt and crumble it.
Whisk the egg, yoghurt and olive oil.
Add the flour and baking powder and mix just until combined.
Add the carrot and cheese and divide between the tins.
Bake for 20 minutes; a toothpick should come out clean.
Add the finely chopped spinach and cook for 2 minutes; let cool.
Cut the filo sheet into 4 cm squares.
Put a little filling in the middle of each square and pinch the corners together to close.
Boil in boiling water for 8 minutes until the dough is soft; drain.
When lukewarm, serve with yoghurt; halve the dumplings if needed.
Preheat the oven to 180°C; line a small loaf tin with baking paper.
Mash the ripe banana and whisk with the egg.
Finely grate the apple and carrot and add them.
Pour into the tin and bake for 30 minutes; a toothpick inserted in the middle should come out clean.
Cut the courgette and carrot into thin sticks; the carrot must be thin so it softens in time.
Toss the vegetables with olive oil and arrange on the tray; place the salmon in the middle.
Bake for 15 minutes until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily.
The carrot should be soft enough to crush with a finger; if not, bake 5 more minutes.
Flake the salmon and serve with the vegetables.
Trim the ends and strings of the beans, wash them and cut into 1 cm pieces.
Stir the grated tomato in the olive oil for 2 minutes.
Add the beans and water; cook covered over low heat for 25 minutes.
The beans should be soft enough to crush with a finger.
Soak the oats in the milk for 5 minutes to soften.
Peel and slice the ripe banana and add it.
Blend for 30–40 seconds until smooth.
Rinse the boiled pasta in cold water and drain.
Wash and peel the cucumber and dice it small.
Soak the white cheese in water for 1 hour to remove salt; dice it small.
Mix the pasta, cucumber and cheese with the olive oil.
Serve immediately or keep in the fridge for 1 day.
Knead the mince with the breadcrumbs; wash your hands after touching raw meat.
With wet hands, form walnut-sized, slightly flat meatballs.
Peel the potato, dice it small and toss with olive oil.
Arrange the meatballs and potatoes spaced out on the tray and bake for 25 minutes, turning halfway.
The potato should be soft enough to crush with a finger.
Break the meatballs into small pieces and serve lukewarm.
Bring the chicken to the boil with the water and skim off the foam; cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Wash the rice; chop the carrot small.
Add the rice and carrot; cook for 20 minutes until the rice is very soft.
Take out the chicken, shred it finely and return it to the pan.
Cut the flatbread into rounds using a glass.
Chop the pepper and mushroom very finely; cook the mushroom in a pan for 2 minutes until its liquid evaporates.
Spread the rounds with grated tomato; sprinkle with the vegetables and cheese.
Knead the flour, olive oil and water into a smooth dough; rest for 10 minutes.
Roll the dough out 2–3 mm thick on baking paper; sprinkle with sesame and press it in with the rolling pin.
Cut into small squares and prick each with a fork so they don't puff up.
Bake for 15 minutes until lightly golden at the edges.
Cool completely on the tray; they become crisp as they cool.
Because of sesame allergy, if giving for the first time start with a small amount and watch.
Keep in a closed jar for 5 days.
